deep.reconstruction:
This page contains no calculations. It continues the philosophical fragment 'Antinomien' begun on the previous page (folio 75r, headed '7 / Antinomien (zu p. 6)'). That page set out a table of Kant-style antinomies. On the 'Thesis' side are the finite and representable (vorstellbar). On the 'Antithesis' side are the infinite and 'systems of concepts lying at the limit of the representable' (Begriffssysteme an der Grenze des Vorstellbaren). It then began a section 'Allgemeines Verhältniss der Begriffssysteme der Thesis und Antithesis' (general relation between the concept systems of thesis and antithesis).

The page completes the description of the limit method (Grenzmethode), which Riemann says Newton used to found the calculus and which the best mathematicians since about 1800 accept as the only reliable method. The method replaces a continuous transition, from one value of a quantity to another, one place to another, or one determination of a concept to another, with three steps:
(i) make the transition through a finite number n of intermediate stages;
(ii) let n grow;
(iii) do this so that all distances between consecutive stages tend to zero.
In modern terms: take a partition x_0 < x_1 < ... < x_n of the transition, form the finite (discrete) object, and pass to the limit as the mesh max_k |x_k - x_{k-1}| tends to 0. This is the scheme behind Cauchy/Riemann sums and difference-to-derivative limits.

Riemann then applies this mathematical scheme as an analogy for metaphysics:
(a) The concept systems of the antithesis (infinite, timeless, etc.) are fixed only by negative predicates. They are not positively representable.
(b) Because no complete representation of them is possible, they cannot be investigated directly.
(c) They can, however, be treated as limits of the representable. One builds a representable concept system that turns into the given one purely by changing its quantitative relations (Größenverhältnisse). Like the mesh going to zero, the structure of the system stays the same in the passage to the limit.
(d) In the limit case itself, some correlative concepts lose their representability: precisely those that mediate relations between other concepts.

The mathematical analogue (my interpretation, not on the page) is that intermediate points and finite steps disappear in the continuum limit, while the formal relations are kept.

No formula appears. The only mathematical content is the verbal definition of passage to the limit via refinement of finite partitions.
errors: No mathematical errors, since there is no computation.

Historically arguable: Riemann credits Newton with founding calculus on the limit method. Newton's 'prime and ultimate ratios' are indeed a limit conception, but rigorous limit foundations are usually credited to Cauchy (1821) and Bolzano. Riemann's phrase 'since the beginning of this century' implicitly acknowledges this later rigorization.
The verbal description requires all step sizes to go to zero (mesh → 0). Merely letting the number of stages grow would not suffice; Riemann states the condition correctly.

results.what: Verbal definition of the limit method: replace a continuous transition by finitely many intermediate stages, then increase their number so that all consecutive gaps tend to zero.
results.modern_name: Limit of partitions with mesh → 0 (the scheme behind Riemann/Cauchy sums and the ε-δ foundation of analysis)
results.usually_credited_to: Newton (prime and ultimate ratios, 1687); rigorous form Cauchy 1821, Bolzano

results.what: Philosophical use of the limit method: the antithesis concepts (infinite, timeless) are treated as limits of representable concept systems obtained by changing only quantitative relations, with the relation-mediating correlative concepts losing representability in the limit.
results.modern_name: Riemann's epistemological 'limit concepts' / Grenzbegriffe; related to Herbart's theory of concepts
results.usually_credited_to: Bernhard Riemann (philosophical fragment 'Antinomien', printed in the Gesammelte Werke edited by Weber and Dedekind, 1876/1892)

The mathematical content is a standard verbal description of the limit method.

checkable.asserts: Illustration of the limit method: a finite subdivision into n equal steps of width 1/n, with n → oo, gives the integral of x**2 on [0,1] = 1/3 (result should be 0).
With equal subdivision, the distance between consecutive intermediate stages tends to 0 as the number of stages grows (result 0).
Difference quotient over finer steps tends to the derivative, another instance of the limit method (result 0).
